anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after form-submit gating, local-event dispatch, asynchronous scheduling, browser environment collection, input normalization and projection preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable browser fingerprint value rather than merely collecting navigator/screen/canvas/media inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

primary_anchor.source_export: private reducer returned by createFingerprintReducer and selected through exported u(tuple, context)
primary_anchor.why: Constructs the requested bf_ browser fingerprint value from normalized browser evidence and the selected active reducer recipe.
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only: the canonical anchor answer is captured_span plus answer_function as declared in the captured bundle slice. source_function is a private maintainer mapping into src/.
primary_anchor.naming_note: source_function differs from answer_function after obfuscation; graders must match captured_span (hash/offset), not the source-side identifier string.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle (hash/offset/complete function body). Agents only see captures, so the standard answer identifier is primary_anchor.answer_function, not source_function.

A returned function name is scored against answer_function in the captured corpus. source_function is a private maintainer label and is not something an agent can know unless the bundle still exposes that exact identifier.
Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from raw browser-feature collection, routing, input preparation, wrapper, sink, core utility and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.

role_oracle.why: Constructs the requested bf_ browser fingerprint value from normalized browser evidence and the selected active reducer recipe.
Checks that the active tuple contains the browser-specific evidence keys required for the real bf_ branch.
Formats the mixed reducer state into the short body used by the bf_ value, but it is generic below the anchor.
Serializes normalized tuple rows into reducer text before target-specific mixing.
Calls the selected reducer; it is a wrapper around the anchor rather than the constructor itself.
Builds the submit listener for the fingerprint form and gates the flow on the armed consent state.
Routes the browser.fingerprint form-submit envelope into the new local event path.
Moves the envelope through a DOM CustomEvent boundary before route continuation.
Crosses Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and MutationObserver boundaries before collection.
Collects navigator, screen, CSS/media, canvas and timezone evidence and forwards the tuple.
Routes the collected tuple into downstream middleware after e4; it is path code, not value construction.
Projects the tuple, prepares register/transit context, calls the selected reducer, and forwards the already constructed value.
Places the already constructed value into the browser_fingerprint payload field.
Updates the DOM and emits console.log; it receives the completed browser_fingerprint value.
Handles unknown actions and never produces the target browser_fingerprint observable.

scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span
scoring_policy.decoy_policy: bf-like values emitted outside action browser.fingerprint and field browser_fingerprint score zero unless the submitted function is the primary anchor or an explicitly listed role.
scoring_policy.dynamic_path_summary: select #fingerprintMode strict -> check #entropyConsent -> submit #fingerprintForm -> b1 submitPipeline -> c2 -> g6 CustomEvent -> h7/i8/j9 -> f5 async scheduler -> e4 collector -> k1/k2/w* -> m0 -> browserFingerprintDigest -> n0 console wrapper

oracle_notes: The visible page interaction is a form flow, not a single button click.
The captured corpus remains a single obfuscated main-thread bundle with no source map.
The primary answer should be the complete captured function _0x49f90a, not the enclosing factory _0x568abc unless the evaluator explicitly accepts enclosing-function expansion.
The form submit handler, router, CustomEvent bridge, async scheduler, browser evidence collector, projection caller and console sink are necessary path code but score below the anchor.
near_miss_not_accepted: generic formatter or hash helper only
